Thanks for the help in advance

messages.author: 0c0915d54307a5d8
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: R script for nested design MANOVA
parts:
Hi Mitra,

I don't have much experience with MANOVAs, but you might want to try the function "adonis" from the "vegan" package. It is a more robust, non-parametric alternative to MANOVA. Because I don't know what your data look like, I can't provide you with a script to run it, but in general, you would run:

library(vegan)

adonis(formula = sppeciesmatrix ~ variable, strata = blockingvariable, data = environmentalmatrix)

Hello Rosemary,

Appreciate your direction and thanks for taking your time to answer my question. I've also heard abt Permutational MANOVA, Using Distance Matrices which is comparable with ADONIS. However, I had no clue if we can apply it for analysing an aspect in soil properties. I thought this only works when we explain the communities with feasible changes of environmental variables.

Here is a short description on my data,

I do have soil physio-chemical data (N, C/N, pH...) which are independent variables. I also have some diversity matrices and indices, and phyla taxonomy as the dependent variables. The experiment has been conducted in a sloping farmland (Up- and Foot-slope) under split split plot design.  

Which whole or main plots have received contour ridges and Reduced tillage
Sub plots  received Residue management including cowpea and Residue management excluding cowpea
Sub-sub plots contain three dosages of Nitrogen (0, 40 and 80 kg/h-1)

Appreciate your help in advance
Best
Mitra

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: R script for nested design MANOVA
parts:
PERMANOVA and MANOVA can be used in pretty much the same way, but the assumptions of PERMANOVA are not as strict, so can be used if the data are not perfectly normal. 

What does your code look like so far? If you are willing to share a sample of your data I might be able to be more help. 

Since you have multiple levels of nesting in your design, you want to constrain the permutations of your PerMANOVA using the "how" funciton. It sounds like the formula you are trying to set up should look something like this:

h1 <- how(within = Within(type = "series"), plots = Plots(strata = subplots, type = "series"), blocks = mainplot)
adonis(diversitymatrix ~ N + C/N + pH, strata = plot, method = h1) 

See if this explanation helps at all.
https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-ecology/2013-February/003595.html

Hi Rosemary,
Million thanks for the info and the useful link.  This code  looks perfect though I need the split split plot design.  I am trying to adapt the code to a similar one

split-split-plot experiment. here is my experimental design; 
12 plots, 2 contour ridge (CR) and reduced tillage(RT) , 
2 residue management with and without Cow pea (R+CP and R-CP), 
3 N dosages (0,40,80) (N0,N40,N80) of which received and four Rep
Each plot was split into "CT" and "RT" within each CR there were two subplots, 
2 "R+CP" and "R-CP" and within each subplots there were 2 sub-subplots ("N0","N40","N80")

adonis(invert.he1 ~ Treatment*tillage*CP+Plot, method="bray", strata=Plot, perm=999)
Plot_tillage <- interaction(Plot,tillage) adonis(invert.he1 ~ Treatment*tillage*cp+Plot_tillage, method="bray", strata=Plot_tillage, perm=999)
adonis(invert.he1 ~ tillage * CP, perm = 999, strata = Plot)

h1 <- how(within = Within(type = "series"), plots = Plots(strata = subplots, type = "series"), blocks = mainplot)
adonis(diversitymatrix ~ N + C/N + pH, strata = plot, method = h1)

Thanks for your help
Mitra
